`# Shell Scripting with GitHub Integration`

`A DevOps project that uses shell scripting and the GitHub REST API to audit who has access to a GitHub repository — useful when a team member resigns and you need to review or revoke their access.`

`## 📌 Overview`

`Instead of logging into GitHub every time to check repository access, this project automates the process using a shell script that talks to the **GitHub REST API**.`

`You can write this automation in **Bash, Python, or any language** that can make HTTP requests — the goal is the same: retrieve repository access information programmatically.`

`## 🧠 Concepts`

`### What is an API?`  
``An **API (Application Programming Interface)** lets you interact with an application programmatically instead of through a UI. GitHub exposes a **REST API** that you can call using tools like `curl` or Python's `requests` module to read and modify data in your repositories.``

`### Why DevOps engineers care`  
``- DevOps engineers **consume APIs** daily (e.g., `boto3` for AWS, GitHub API for repos).``  
`- Developers **document APIs** so others know how to use them.`  
`- GitHub publishes full [API documentation](https://docs.github.com/rest) showing exactly which endpoint to call for issues, repos, access, etc.`

`## 🎯 Project Goal`

`In real DevOps environments, teams maintain many GitHub repos across microservices. This project ensures:`

`1. You can **list all users with access** to a repo.`  
`2. You can **identify who has read vs. write access**.`  
`3. You can **revoke access** when someone leaves (via script or manually).`

``> **Note:** In open-source projects, access is often tracked in a public `OWNERS` file. In private orgs, access is managed through **repo/org settings**.``

`## 🚀 Setup Steps`

`### 1. Launch an AWS instance`  
`- Create an **Ubuntu** EC2 instance using a public key.`  
``- Connect via SSH using your `.pem` file (or `.ppk` for PuTTY/MobaXterm).``

`### 2. Install prerequisites`  
```` ```bash ````  
`sudo yum install jq -y`  
```` ``` ````  
``> If you get `jq: command not found`, this installs it.``  
![][image1]![][image2]

`### 3. Clone the repository`  
```` ```bash ````  
`git clone <your-repo-url>`  
`cd github-api -  Here is the sample screenshot`  
![][image3]  
```` ``` ````

`### 4. Export your GitHub credentials`  
`Generate a **Personal Access Token** from GitHub → *Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens*.`

```` ```bash ````  
`export username="your-github-username"`  
`export token="your-personal-access-token"`  
```` ``` ````

`### 5. Make the script executable`  
```` ```bash ````  
`chmod +x list_users.sh`  
```` ``` ````

`### 6. Run the script`  
```` ```bash ````  
`./list_users.sh <org-name> <repo-name>`  
```` ``` ````

**`**Example:**`**  
```` ```bash ````  
`./list_users.sh devops_by_examples python`  
```` ``` ````  
``- `devops_by_examples` → organization name``  
``- `python` → repository name``

`## 📤 Output`

`The script prints the list of users with access to the specified repository.`

![][image4]

`## 🔁 Reusing the Script`

`To check a different repo, just change the org and repo names:`

```` ```bash ````  
`./list_users.sh <new-org> <new-repo>`  
```` ``` ````

`## 🧪 Practice Setup`

`Want to try this on your own?`  
`1. Go to GitHub and create a **free organization**.`  
`2. Create a new repository inside it.`  
`3. Follow the setup steps above and run the script against your own org/repo.`

`## 🧩 Key Takeaway`

`> **If you cannot do something through the GitHub UI, you cannot do it via the API either.**`

`The API mirrors UI permissions — it's just faster and scriptable.`

`## 📋 Quick Reference`

`| Step | Command |`  
`|------|---------|`  
``| Install jq | `sudo yum install jq -y` |``  
``| Clone repo | `git clone <repo-url>` |``  
``| Set permissions | `chmod +x list_users.sh` |``  
``| Export username | `export username="your-username"` |``  
``| Export token | `export token="your-token"` |``  
``| Run script | `./list_users.sh <org> <repo>` |``

`## 🔐 Security Reminder`

`- **Never commit your token** to a repository.`  
`- Use environment variables or a secrets manager.`  
`- Revoke tokens you no longer need at: https://github.com/settings/tokens`
